name: WIP and retention
summary: Keeps the work-in-progress position for each construction job (billed against earned) and drafts progress claims in Xero. Crons read and draft: a progress claim is a DRAFT invoice until a person approves its authorisation and email, and reminders for overdue invoices wait for approval too. Xero is the only platform with mapped invoice operations for this job, so it is the only adapter.

covered_by.job-set-up: settings (contract value and percent complete per job)
covered_by.cost-capture: not covered (cost to date is not read from Xero yet)
covered_by.variation-tracking: not covered (judgment, stays with the business)

covered_by.record-keeping: wip-snapshot (kept in the store; Xero stays the record)
not covered (SimPro is not in the kit's platform list)

crons.name: wip-snapshot
crons.summary: Weekly (Monday morning in eastern Australia): each job's billed-to-date against its earned value, kept in the store.

crons.name: progress-claim
crons.summary: Daily: a job whose claim interval has passed gets a DRAFT progress invoice in Xero, and one approval to authorise and email it.

crons.name: chase
crons.summary: Daily: an authorised invoice past due gets its next reminder queued for approval (22:30 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads of invoices, and a Xero invoice in DRAFT. Authorising an invoice and emailing it (a progress claim or a reminder) change what the client sees, so they are live operations and wait for a person.

xero.covers: invoice reads for the billing position, DRAFT progress claim invoices, authorise and email for approval, overdue reminders

gaps: Buildxact: the kit maps only its sign-in for this job. Estimates, jobs, WIP reports, completion-percent invoices and retention have no operations, so there is no adapter. Its help pages describe all of these, so this is the first platform to map.
MYOB: the kit maps time-billing activities and a read of sales invoices. The pages read are for professional time billing, not construction progress, retention or WIP, so there is no adapter.
Simpro: not in the kit's platform list. Job costs and the Monday WIP report built from SimPro data stay manual.
Cost to date: the snapshot compares billing with earned value only. Job cost is not read from Xero until a demo company confirms the shape of the profit and loss report by tracking category.

Retention: each claim records the retention it holds in the store, but the Xero invoice carries the gross claim. Netting retention off needs a negative invoice line, which is not confirmed on a demo company. Retention owed to subcontractors and retention release at completion are not covered.
Percent complete comes from settings (the owner or the site report). The workflow does not read measurements or site photos.
Variations, job set-up and month-end close are judgment steps that stay with the business. Settings hold the result.
Invoice reads cover the first page only (up to 100 invoices per call). Paging beyond that is not built.
Reminders: Xero's email sends the invoice itself, so a reminder is the invoice email again with no custom wording. A rejected reminder still counts as sent for the schedule.
Tax: lines post with the sales account's default tax. Confirm that setting with the owner before the first claim is authorised.
Cross-workflow: the invoicing workflow in finance-admin also drafts Xero invoices. Running both on one business could draft two invoices for the same job. No cross-workflow dedupe is built.
The workflow is docs-only until a Xero demo company proves it against real data.
A rejected progress claim is not billed, so its progress is claimed again on the next claim. Its DRAFT invoice stays in Xero and has to be voided or deleted by hand.
